pages.text: $(italic)$(#6b5a45)Files go into a data pack; $(#8a5a2b)/reload$()$(italic)$(#6b5a45) applies them. The in-game scanner is the easiest way in.$()$(br2)Three ways in: the $(bold)scanner$() exports a house in-game without touching any file;
a $(bold)data pack$() changes buildings, element values, recipes, spells and chests with JSON;$(br) the $(bold)API$() is for mod authors writing Java.

Into your save's $(#8a5a2b)<world>/datapacks/<pack>/data/<namespace>/<category>/$(). Any namespace will do;$(br) you only need $(#8a5a2b)wandscape$() with the same file name to override something the mod ships.
pages.title: Where the files go

pages.text: Buildings go in $(#8a5a2b)buildings/<pack>/$(), element values in $(#8a5a2b)element_mappings/$(), recipes and scrolls in $(#8a5a2b)cr$(br)aft_recipes/$(), spells and circles in $(#8a5a2b)magic_spells/$() and $(#8a5a2b)magic_circles/$(), wild chests in $(#8a5a2b)explorati$(br)on_regions/$(), balance numbers in $(#8a5a2b)wandscape_balance.json$(). This is where the scanner exports.
Data packs follow the $(bold)world$(): every save carries its own, and scanner exports live only inside it. The mod's own content sit$(br)s in the jar.
pages.title: World or global

pages.text: The settings centre is $(bold)global$() ($(#8a5a2b)config/wandscape-*.toml$()): server-side keys are shared, client-side ones affect $(br)only your machine. Scanner presets are global too.
